requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop test behaviour operation IS the operation used to stop the execution of a test component by itself or by another test component.
requirements.original: The stop test behaviour operation is used to stop the execution of a test component by itself or by another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The stop test behaviour operation has the syntax `stop` | ( ( ObjectReference | `mtc` | `self` ) "." `stop` ) | ( `all component` "." `stop` ).
requirements.original:
stop | 
  ( ( ObjectReference | mtc | self ) "." stop ) |
  ( all component "." stop )

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component CAN stop the execution of its own currently running test behaviour or of the test behaviour running on another test component by using the `stop` operation.
requirements.original: By using the `stop` test component statement a test component can stop the execution of its own currently running test behaviour or the execution of the test behaviour running on another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the stopped component is another test component
requirements.canonical: When a test component stops the behaviour running on another test component, the component to be stopped SHALL be identified by its component reference.
requirements.original: If a component does not stop its own behaviour, but the behaviour running on another test component in the test system, the component to be stopped has to be identified by using its component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component MAY stop its own behaviour by a simple `stop` execution statement or by addressing itself in the `stop` operation, e.g. with `self.stop`.
requirements.original: A component can stop its own behaviour by using a simple `stop` execution statement (see clause 19.9) or by addressing itself in the `stop` operation, e.g. by using the `self` operation.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: Each of the `create`, `start`, `running`, `done` and `killed` operations IS applicable to PTCs only.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: While the `create`, `start`, `running`, `done` and `killed` operations can be used for PTC(s) only, the `stop` operation can also be applied to the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `stop` operation CAN also be applied to the MTC.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: While the `create`, `start`, `running`, `done` and `killed` operations can be used for PTC(s) only, the `stop` operation can also be applied to the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Stopping a test component IS the explicit form of terminating the execution of its currently running behaviour.
requirements.original: Stopping a test component is the explicit form of terminating the execution of the currently running behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: A test component behaviour IS also terminated when its execution reaches the end of the test behaviour started on the component or an explicit `return` statement.
requirements.original: A test component behaviour terminates also by completing its execution upon reaching the end of the test behaviour that is started on this component or by an explicit `return` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-stop
requirements.canonical: Termination of a test component behaviour by reaching its end or by an explicit `return` statement IS called implicit stop.
requirements.original: This termination is also called implicit stop.

requirements.subject: ent:implicit-stop
requirements.canonical: An implicit stop IS equivalent in its effects to an explicit stop.
requirements.original: The implicit stop has the same effects as an explicit stop, i.e. the global verdict is updated with the local verdict of the stopped test component (see clause 24).

requirements.subject: ent:global-verdict
requirements.canonical: When a test component stops (implicitly or explicitly), the global verdict IS updated with the local verdict of the stopped test component.
requirements.original: The implicit stop has the same effects as an explicit stop, i.e. the global verdict is updated with the local verdict of the stopped test component (see clause 24).

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.condition: the stopped test component is the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the stopped test component is the MTC, the resources of all existing PTCs SHALL be released.
requirements.original: If the stopped test component is the MTC, resources of all existing PTCs shall be released, the PTCs shall be removed from the test system and the test case shall terminate (see clause 26.1).

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.condition: the stopped test component is the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the stopped test component is the MTC, all existing PTCs SHALL be removed from the test system.
requirements.original: If the stopped test component is the MTC, resources of all existing PTCs shall be released, the PTCs shall be removed from the test system and the test case shall terminate (see clause 26.1).

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.condition: the stopped test component is the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the stopped test component is the MTC, the test case SHALL terminate.
requirements.original: If the stopped test component is the MTC, resources of all existing PTCs shall be released, the PTCs shall be removed from the test system and the test case shall terminate (see clause 26.1).

requirements.subject: ent:non-alive-ptc
requirements.canonical: Stopping a non-alive-type test component (implicitly or explicitly) SHALL destroy it.
requirements.original: Stopping a non-alive-type test component (implicitly or explicitly) shall destroy it and all resources associated with the test component shall be released.

requirements.subject: ent:non-alive-ptc
requirements.canonical: When a non-alive-type test component is stopped, all resources associated with it SHALL be released.
requirements.original: Stopping a non-alive-type test component (implicitly or explicitly) shall destroy it and all resources associated with the test component shall be released.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: Stopping an alive-type component SHALL stop only its currently running behaviour.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component shall stop the currently running behaviour only but the component continues to exist and can execute new behaviour (started on it using the start operation).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: A stopped alive-type component SHALL continue to exist.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component shall stop the currently running behaviour only but the component continues to exist and can execute new behaviour (started on it using the start operation).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: A stopped alive-type component CAN execute a new behaviour started on it by the start test component operation.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component shall stop the currently running behaviour only but the component continues to exist and can execute new behaviour (started on it using the start operation).

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, every component variable, component timer and port IS unchanged in its value, contents or state.
requirements.original: Stopping an alive-type component means that all variables, timers and ports declared in the component type definition of the alive-type component keep their value, contents or state.

requirements.subject: ent:local-verdict
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, its local verdict IS kept unchanged.
requirements.original: Furthermore, the local verdict of the component keeps its value.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: When an alive-type component is stopped, every active default IS automatically deactivated.
requirements.original: In contrast to that, all active defaults are automatically deactivated when the alive-type component is stopped.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component SHALL be left in a consistent state after its behaviour is stopped.
requirements.original: The component shall be left in a consistent state after stopping its behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.condition: the behaviour of an alive-type component is stopped during assignment to an already bound variable
requirements.canonical: If the behaviour of an alive-type component is stopped while a new value is assigned to an already bound variable, the variable SHALL remain bound after the component is stopped (with the old or the new value).
requirements.original: For example, if the behaviour of an alive-type component is stopped during assigning a new value to an already bound variable, the variable shall remain bound after the component is stopped (with the old or the new value).

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.condition: the component is stopped during re-starting an already running timer
requirements.canonical: If an alive-type component is stopped while re-starting an already running timer, the timer SHALL be left in the running state after termination of the behaviour.
requirements.original: Similarly, if the component is stopped during re-starting an already running timer, the timer shall be left in the running state after termination of the behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all component` keyword SHALL be used with the `stop` operation by the MTC only.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

ambiguity.issue: The keyword is called 'the all keyword'; the actual construct is `all component`.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.stop` operation IS the stopping of every running PTC, excluding the MTC itself.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

requirements.subject: ent:ptc
requirements.canonical: A PTC CAN stop the test case execution by stopping the MTC.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: A PTC can stop the test case execution by stopping the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a stop test behaviour operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a stop test behaviour operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The kill test component operation IS the operation used to destroy a test component by itself or by another test component.
requirements.original: The kill test component operation is used to destroy a component by itself or by another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: On a non-alive test component, the `kill` operation IS equivalent in its results to the `stop` operation.
requirements.original: Kill and stop on a non-alive component have the same results, while they differ for alive components: stopping an alive components stops the test behaviour only, the test component continues to exist.

requirements.subject: ent:alive-type-ptc
requirements.canonical: Stopping an alive-type component IS the termination of its test behaviour only, while the test component continues to exist.
requirements.original: Kill and stop on a non-alive component have the same results, while they differ for alive components: stopping an alive components stops the test behaviour only, the test component continues to exist.

ambiguity.issue: 'alive components' is used instead of 'alive-type components'.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: Killing a test component IS the destruction of that test component.
requirements.original: Killing a test component destroys the test component.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The kill test component operation has the syntax `kill` | ( ( ObjectReference | `mtc` | `self` ) "." `kill` ) | ( `all component` "." `kill` ).
requirements.original:
kill | 
  ( ( ObjectReference | mtc | self ) "." kill ) |
  ( all component "." kill )

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation applied on a test component IS terminating the execution of the currently running behaviour of that component, if any.
requirements.original: The kill operation applied on a test component stops the execution of the currently running behaviour - if any - of that component and frees all resources associated to it (including all port connections of the killed component) and removes the component from the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation applied on a test component IS freeing all resources associated with that component, including all its port connections.
requirements.original: The kill operation applied on a test component stops the execution of the currently running behaviour - if any - of that component and frees all resources associated to it (including all port connections of the killed component) and removes the component from the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation applied on a test component IS removing the component from the test system.
requirements.original: The kill operation applied on a test component stops the execution of the currently running behaviour - if any - of that component and frees all resources associated to it (including all port connections of the killed component) and removes the component from the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation MAY be applied by a test component on itself by a simple `kill` statement or by `self.kill`.
requirements.original: The kill operation can be applied on the current test component itself by a simple kill statement or by addressing itself using the self operation in conjunction with the kill operation.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation MAY be applied to another test component.
requirements.original: The kill operation can also be applied to another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: the kill operation is applied to another test component
requirements.canonical: When the `kill` operation is applied to another test component, the component to be killed SHALL be addressed using its component reference.
requirements.original: In this case the component to be killed shall be addressed using its component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.condition: the kill operation is applied on the MTC
requirements.canonical: If the `kill` operation is applied on the MTC (e.g. `mtc.kill`), the test case IS terminated.
requirements.original: If the kill operation is applied on the MTC, e.g. mtc.kill, it terminates the test case.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `all component` keyword SHALL be used with the `kill` operation by the MTC only.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop and kill all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

ambiguity.issue: The keyword is called 'the all keyword'; the actual construct is `all component`.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.kill` operation IS stopping and killing every PTC, excluding the MTC itself.
requirements.original: The all keyword can be used by the MTC only in order to stop and kill all running PTCs but the MTC itself.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'all running PTCs', while EXAMPLE 2 says all (alive-type and normal) PTCs, which includes inactive and stopped alive-type PTCs. The example reading is chosen.
readings: The `all component.kill` operation IS stopping and killing every existing PTC (running, inactive or stopped), excluding the MTC.
The `all component.kill` operation IS stopping and killing only the PTCs that are currently running a behaviour, excluding the MTC.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a kill test component operation SHALL be of component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a kill test component operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of component type and shall not resolve to a template.
